guide.summary: Royal castles, museums, food markets and a harbourside art district, with breakfast spots, lunch and dinner tables, bakeries, coffee and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Save Mondays for the National Museum of Denmark, which opens daily 10:00–17:00, because Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, Louisiana, Copenhagen Contemporary and Thorvaldsens Museum close on Mondays, as does Rosenborg Castle from 2 November.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, Louisiana, Copenhagen Contemporary and Thorvaldsens Museum are closed on Mondays, and Rosenborg Castle is closed Mondays from 2 November. Kunsthal Charlottenborg closes on Tuesdays instead.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Rosenborg Castle saves you 10 kroner per ticket bought online and Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek 10%, while the National Museum of Denmark charges 135 DKK online against 150 DKK. Louisiana needs no time slot, and online tickets are valid for a visit within a year.

toolkit.label: Free entry
toolkit.copy: Thorvaldsens Museum is free for everyone on Wednesdays, Kunsthal Charlottenborg from 17.00 on Wednesdays, and Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek on the last Wednesday of each month. Under-18s enter free at the National Museum of Denmark, Louisiana and Rundetaarn.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Ruby has a minimum entry age of 21, and Rosenborg Castle allows no food or drink in the castle or Treasury. Rundetaarn has no lift and says it is not well suited to wheelchairs and pushchairs.

guide.dek: Build each day around one museum's opening hours, since closing days differ, and book the tasting-menu dinners well ahead.
intro: Copenhagen's historic sights are easy to combine on foot. The National Museum of Denmark at Ny Vestergade 10 opens every day from 10:00 to 17:00; adult tickets cost 150 DKK, or 135 DKK online, they stay valid for a year, and under-18s go free. Rosenborg Castle on Øster Voldgade opens Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 16:00 from 2 November, and buying online saves you 10 kroner a ticket. Rundetaarn on Købmagergade stays open until 21:00 on Mondays and Tuesdays through the winter, when its observatory runs telescope evenings, and adult entry costs 60 DKK.

Several art museums close on Mondays, so plan around that. Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek on Dantes Plads opens Tuesday to Sunday, until 21:00 on Thursdays, and is free on the last Wednesday of each month; its exhibition The Power of Fashion in the Roman Empire runs until 29 March 2027. Thorvaldsens Museum is free for everyone on Wednesdays. Designmuseum Danmark on Bredgade shows Henrik Vibskov: The Exhibition until 21 February 2027, and Kunsthal Charlottenborg at Nyhavn 2, which closes on Tuesdays, has three exhibitions running to the same date.

Louisiana Museum of Modern Art at Gl. Strandvej 13 in Humlebæk needs no time slot. It opens Tuesday to Friday until 22:00 and weekends until 18:00, and you need a ticket even for its café, shop or sculpture park. Its Tracey Emin exhibition runs until 18 April 2027. Back in the city, Refshaleøen pairs Reffen's street food, open daily from 11.30, with Copenhagen Contemporary, which opens until 21:00 on Thursdays and shows Camille Henrot's Paper Planes until 31 December 2026 alongside a permanent James Turrell work.

For food, Torvehallerne on Frederiksborggade serves breakfast and bakery items from 07:00, and the GRØD porridge stall there opens at 7:00 on weekdays. Restaurant Schønnemann on Hauser Plads serves lunch daily from 11:30, runs a Christmas season from 12 November to 23 December 2026, then closes until 5 January 2027. Geranium takes bookings up to three months ahead, with a 1,500 DKK deposit per guest. For drinks, Lidkoeb on Vesterbrogade is closed on Sundays, and Ruby on Nybrogade admits guests aged 21 and over.
summaryCards: Pair the National Museum of Denmark, open daily 10:00–17:00, with Rundetaarn and Rosenborg Castle, both a short walk from Torvehallerne.
Start with porridge at GRØD in Torvehallerne or a pastry from Juno the Bakery on Århusgade, then the Botanical Garden, open from 8:30.
Check Monday closures at Glyptotek, Louisiana and Copenhagen Contemporary, and book Geranium up to three months ahead with its 1,500 DKK per-guest deposit.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The input lists were entirely generic, so all 28 places were added as candidates. Some places were published only partially: Tivoli Gardens' homepage gave no opening hours, Mikkeller Bar Viktoriagade listed no hours, Designmuseum Danmark showed only today's hours, Rosenborg Castle's page showed hours only from 2 November, and Copenhagen Zoo's only for 25–31 October 2026. Noma's site says it returned to Copenhagen in August 2026 without an exact date. Kødbyens Fiskebar, Ruby, Geranium, Coffee Collective and Andersen Bakery showed hours or booking but no dated 2026 content. The Botanical Garden's Palm House is under renovation, with parts closed at times. Sites that could not be read: SMK (title only), Christiansborg Palace (placeholder), Den Blå Planet, Hija de Sanchez, Alouette and Copenhagen Coffee Lab (certificate errors), Atelier September (403), Hart Bageri (TLS error), La Cabra, Prolog and Apollo Bar (429 rate limits), and Duck and Cover (DNS failure).
